title: Make each billing job run as its own tenant

blocks.text: The billing service keeps one schema per tenant. Its jobs run on a shared thread pool, and the repositories call `TenantContext.current()` to choose the schema. Last month an invoice run for a small tenant wrote three invoices into another tenant's schema. The job that ran just before it on the same pool thread had failed halfway with "ledger locked". Transfers between two tenants run one job inside another: the outer job for the payer, a nested one for the payee.

Write `runAs(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/TenantContext.java`. When you're done, a job sees its own tenant while it runs, and every job after it on the same thread sees what it should: no tenant after a job, even after a failed one, and the outer tenant again when a nested job ends. The job's exception still reaches the caller. About ten lines in total.
The tests run the jobs on a pool with a single thread, so each job runs on the thread the one before it used.

cases.says: inside runAs, current() answers the job's tenant
two threads inside runAs at the same time each see their own tenant
after a job ends, the next job on the same pool thread sees no tenant
after a job fails, the next job on the same pool thread sees no tenant
when a runAs inside another runAs ends, the outer job's tenant is current again

origin.section: A ThreadLocal Value Belongs to the Thread, So a Pool Hands It to the Next Task

concepts: A ThreadLocal value lives as long as its thread, so on a pool it must be removed in finally, or restored to the outer value when calls nest, or the next task on that thread sees it.
